outcome: clinical presentation (amenorrhea, abdominal pain, bleeding per vaginum, adnexal tenderness)
morbidity (anemia, blood transfusion requirement, ventilatory or ionotropic support, hemorrhagic shock)
cohort: The study included 60 patients diagnosed with ectopic pregnancy at a tertiary care hospital.
finding: The study found that ectopic pregnancies were most common in primiparous women aged 26-30 years, frequently located at the ampulla, often presented with amenorrhea and abdominal pain, and were associated with significant morbidity including anemia and a 3.3% maternal mortality rate.
mod_finding: A history of previous C-section was identified as a risk factor for ectopic pregnancy in 13.3% of cases.
